title: Thursday, Says Dave
subject: a man in a Salford terrace whose bathroom tap drips all week while the plumber Dave keeps texting 'Thursday', until he starts dancing round the flat to the drip
caption: Madchester baggy revival, late-80s Manchester indie-dance style. A shuffling funky-drummer breakbeat with maracas and tambourine, chiming wah-wah rhythm guitar, a high melodic bass line carrying the hook, a Hammond organ comping on the offbeats. Hazy baggy mix, reverb on the guitars, loose swaying groove. Male lead in a laconic Mancunian half-sung drawl, a few lads joining the chorus. 98 BPM, A major. Sunny, loose and mock-patient. No britpop stadium anthem, no autotune, no trap drums, no EDM drop, no metal distortion.
lyrics:
[Intro - breakbeat, wah guitar and bass]

[Verse 1]
Bathroom tap goes drip all night
Tried a spanner, no dice
Rang the plumber, he's called Dave
Dave says Thursday, Dave's a saint

[Pre-Chorus]
Monday, Tuesday, still it goes
Drip drip drip, the bucket knows

[Chorus]
Thursday, says Dave
Thursday, he swears
Bucket in the bath
And I'm dancing on the stairs

[Verse 2]
Got a rhythm, got a beat
Drip goes kick and I move my feet
Tea towel round my head like a hat
Next door's cat just stares at that

[Chorus]
Thursday, says Dave
Which Thursday, mate?
Bucket's nearly full
And I'm grooving while I wait

[Bridge - organ and maracas]
Washer costs a quid
Dave's van is in Rhyl

[Chorus]
Thursday, says Dave
Here he comes at last
Two minutes with a washer
Now the party's in the past

[Outro - breakbeat fades]
Quiet in the bathroom now
Kind of miss it anyhow
